# dladiv

> Performs complex division in real arithmetic, avoiding unnecessary overflow.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dladiv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dladiv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dladiv( a, b, c, d, p, q ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | Real part of numerator |
| `b` | `number` | Imaginary part of numerator |
| `c` | `number` | Real part of denominator |
| `d` | `number` | Imaginary part of denominator |
| `p` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `p` |
| `q` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the scalars p and q in the above expression |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `d`: The scalars a, b, c, and d in the above expression.
- `q`: The scalars p and q in the above expression.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dladiv.ndarray( a, b, c, d, p, q ) → void
```

Performs complex division in real arithmetic, avoiding unnecessary overflow, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | Real part of numerator |
| `b` | `number` | Imaginary part of numerator |
| `c` | `number` | Real part of denominator |
| `d` | `number` | Imaginary part of denominator |
| `p` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `p` |
| `q` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the scalars p and q in the above expression |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `d`: The scalars a, b, c, and d in the above expression.
- `q`: The scalars p and q in the above expression.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dladiv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLADIV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dladiv.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dladiv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dladiv';

// Using the standard interface:
const p = new Float64Array( 1 );
const q = new Float64Array( 1 );

dladiv( 1, 1, 1.0, 1, p, q );
let out = new Float64Array( [ p[ 0 ], q[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
dladiv.ndarray( 1, 1, 1.0, 1, p, q );
out = new Float64Array( [ p[ 0 ], q[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLADIV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLADIV performs complex division in real arithmetic

$$
a + i \, b
$$

$$
p + i \, q = ---------
$$

$$
c + i \, d
$$

The algorithm is due to Michael Baudin and Robert L. Smith and can be found in the paper "A Robust Complex Division in Scilab"

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
